script.opening_words:
Danielle is standing in her kitchen at
11:00 at night holding her phone up to
the light from the fridge doing math on
a $34 grocery order before she lets
herself hit pay. She's 24. She answers
phones at a physical therapy clinic. She
makes about $50,000 a year and there's a
car with 140,000
miles on it parked outside that she is
actively afraid to ask questions about.
8 years later, Danielle is standing in a
different kitchen. Quartz counters. An
island bigger than
script.ending_words:
it on its own.
We've got a woman standing in a
beautiful kitchen at $300,000 a year to
prove that. The fix was never a bigger
number on a direct deposit, but it's
noticing which game you're actually
playing at your specific income and
making sure the savings rate grows every
time the paycheck does, instead of
quietly getting left behind in the old
kitchen.
Whatever bracket you're standing in
tonight, the rules are different than
you were told, and now you know which
ones actually apply to you.
If this helped, our school community has
more where this came from, and I'll see
you in the next one.
